text:
The SEC's approval of the T. Rowe Price Active Crypto ETF — the first actively managed multi-asset crypto product from a traditional asset manager — marks a structural expansion of institutional access to digital assets beyond passive Bitcoin exposure. Simultaneously, U.S. Congress embedded a CBDC prohibition until 2030 into housing legislation, hardening the regulatory boundary between private crypto and government-issued digital currencies. Bitcoin consolidated in a $65,500–$65,800 channel as the crypto Fear & Greed index registered 22 (Extreme Fear), with the weekly high of $67,200 fading ahead of Chair Warsh's inaugural FOMC press conference.

The S&P 500 gained 0.33% to 7,536 as a reported U.S.-Iran interim deal pushed Brent crude below $80 — a risk-on signal that, paradoxically, failed to lift crypto. The DXY softened to 99.50 on oil shock relief, yet Bitcoin's correlation with equities (30-day r² of 0.61) remains the binding macro constraint. With headline inflation at 4.2% and rates held at 3.50%–3.75%, institutional capital rotation toward AI and semiconductor equities continues to compete directly with crypto for risk-budget allocation.
